motion-tools-and-skills

Tools, agent skills, prompts and starters for making motion graphics with AI agents (Claude Code).

  • Code-rendered motion: Three.js + GSAP, HyperFrames, Remotion, Canvas, WebGL/WebGPU, p5.js.
  • Agent-driven apps: Blender, Unreal Engine, ComfyUI, DaVinci Resolve.
  • The films it is for: launch films, news explainers and music videos, with QA gates, sound, captions and licence notes.

Everything copied here keeps its upstream licence. Every folder has a NOTES.md that says what it does, when to use it, what it needs and what was changed. Where each piece came from is in SOURCES.md.

Start here

  1. Read docs/techniques.md. It distils the shared method behind all of these projects into working rules for our stack.
  2. Pick a skill from the tables below and install it (see Using a skill).
  3. Check docs/reference-only.md before reusing anything that isn't here: it lists useful material that could not be copied, and why.

design/ — brand, type and design systems

Where a film's look comes from, before anything moves. The outputs feed motion tokens, lower thirds, idents and title styles.

  • brand-identity/: two to four logo + type + palette sets from one brief.
    • Measured for contrast, colour blindness, glyph coverage and font licences, and compared as cards.
    • Ends with a guidelines kit, logo files and design tokens for the pick.
  • make-font/: your own OFL font fitted to fonts you like, without tracing their outlines.
  • awwwards-design-md/: an evidence-backed DESIGN.md from any public URL.
  • flexoki/: new. A ready editorial palette (paper and ink, eight accents in 13 steps) as CSS and tokens, with a measured colour-blind-safe chart set.

engineering/ — architecture, engineering and construction

Buildings as the subject, for MAKEENA's real-estate films and AEC explainers. Studies and visualisations only, never engineering advice.

  • build-sequence-film/: a model goes up element by element in build order.
    • One isometric take, with the line drawing warming into colour.
    • 16:9 or 9:16, deterministic frames.
  • brief-to-ifc/: a brief as numbers → a schema-valid IFC4 model for Revit or Archicad.
    • Grid, footings, frame, slabs, core and a facade with windows.
    • Also writes a named GLB for the film.
  • guides/aec-ai-workflows/: nine AEC visualisation workflows (Chiang Ning's pack, linked not copied), the Revit and Archicad MCP servers, and the safety line for structural tools.

tools/ — render, check, edit and finish

Review and analysis

  • headless-render/: review sheets, frame strips, tracked crops and parallel rendering for any time-pure page; GPU probe for headless Chrome.
  • lemo-core/: parallel video render, reading-time check, loudness master with grain, procedural SFX, TTS with a Whisper check, three.js post and CRT passes.
  • sync-check/: sound against picture in a rendered MP4 (off-beat hits, startling jumps).
  • film-analysis/: turn a reference film into cuts, a beat grid and motion heatmaps, and test a finished film for slide-deck feel and empty frames.
  • yt-dlp/: new. Fetch reference films and subtitles for the analysis tools, with the study-not-reuse rules.
  • awwwards-mcp/: award-winning web references, and motion measurement of any page (motion DNA, scroll and hover census, motion-through recordings, GSAP stubs). Install notes only; the server installs from npm.

Sound, voice and captions

  • song-analysis/: song → beat grid, downbeats, sections, per-instrument onsets from separated stems, loudness envelopes, and word-level lyric timing.
  • sound-sheet/: a motion cue sheet → a deterministic SFX stem, every sound derived from the motion; plus a sound-family generator.
  • whisperx/: word-level timestamps for captions and cutting to the voice-over, with Arabic alignment.
  • openverse/: searching openly licensed music and images, and the licence rules for using them.

Editing and finishing

  • auto-editor/: new. Cut silence and dead space, and export the edit as a Resolve, Premiere or Kdenlive timeline. Five skills; tested.
  • davinci-resolve-mcp/: new. Claude drives DaVinci Resolve Studio on Windows: timelines, markers, grades and LUTs, Fusion, render queue, broadcast-legal checks.
  • kdenlive-mcp/: a headless agent editor that assembles a timeline, renders with output checks and exports OTIO for Resolve.
  • open-fusion-mcp/: editable Fusion node graphs in Resolve built by an agent; macOS only for now.
  • effectcraft/: an open After Effects-style compositor with an MCP server; alpha, watch.

3D, depth and camera

  • blender-mcp/: setup notes for the MCP server that lets Claude drive an open Blender (installed with uv, not copied), with its telemetry and safe-mode settings.
  • mesh-pipeline/: our own tested scripts for generated and scanned meshes outside Blender.
    • Tripo text/image → GLB, and a build123d code-CAD prop.
    • PyMeshLab cleanup, xatlas UVs and meshoptimizer LOD chains.
  • mixamo-retarget/: human joints → animated Mixamo character GLB, in numpy, without Blender.
  • tidewater-asset-pipeline/: CC0 sound sourcing and −23 LUFS normalisation; Blender batch retargeting to GLB and decimation.
  • photo-parallax/: our own tested pipeline from one photo to a moving-camera shot.
    • Depth from Depth Anything, Depth Pro 2 or an import; panoptic layers; background fill (OpenCV or SDXL).
    • A time-pure three.js page with dolly, truck, orbit, crane and vertigo moves at any aspect.
    • A commercial-safe path is marked.
  • depth-anything/: depth from one photo for parallax and single-image meshes, with the commercially licensed checkpoints named.
  • threejs-addons/: three.quarks particles (with a seeding recipe for frame-exact renders), pmndrs/postprocessing, Tweakpane.
  • skills/3d-product/references/dsh-blender-modeling/: Blender modelling pitfalls, numeric gates, Blender 5.2 API breaks, three-view calibration, verifier checklist.

Other engines and generators

  • hyperframes-skills/: new. Which of HyperFrames' nine official skills to use when (registry of 450 blocks, reverse-any-video, style-sampling, remotion-to-hyperframes…).
  • raea/: notes for raea, React + TypeScript video, motion graphics and 3D rendered on your own GPU (a possible fifth stack beside Remotion and HyperFrames); FSL licence, young on Windows.
  • tdmcp/: Derivative's official TouchDesigner MCP and skills, for generative and audio-reactive visuals; setup and licence tiers.
  • manim/: maths and diagram explainers in the 3Blue1Brown manner.
  • anidoodle/: hand-drawn art as code in 32 styles, from stills to scored films (a plugin).
  • tegaki/: handwriting animation from any font, Arabic joining included (tested), frame-exact with controlled time.
  • comfyui-piflow/: MiniMax H3 video with audio in 2–4 steps in ComfyUI, with the workflows for our 4090 and 3090.
  • frame-interpolation/: RIFE, in ComfyUI or on the command line, and when not to use it.
  • waoowaoo/: a self-hosted AI film workspace (brief, references, generated images and video on one canvas, models through OpenRouter); preview, Elastic License 2.0.

Beat detection, cut detection, green-screen keying, SFX mixing and a synth score also live inside the skills (listed in tools/README.md).

starters/ — templates to build on

  • tidewater-webgpu-fx/: FFT ocean, physical sky, caustics, lens flare, motion blur and a full post chain in raw WebGPU/WGSL, with headless capture.
  • pdoom-video-engine/: a three.js engine for audio-driven films with adaptive per-tile motion blur, true 4K from a 1080p layout and an HDR post chain.
  • mg-styles-15/: 15 motion-design films with full source, a renderAt(t) render harness and the mgaudio soundtrack toolkit.
  • papermotion/: a paper-cutout film engine with rigs, physics and simulation-driven sound, plus its skill.
  • dioramas/: cinematic 3D pages with volumetric light, reflections and an AgX post stack.
    • Image → 3D assets through fal (Nano Banana 2 → Meshy 7.1).
    • Deterministic video capture of any live-clock page (dioramas, Anatomy figures, React Bits components), with --scale and --clip.
  • hyperframes-motion-library/: 27 parameterised info graphics for explainers (counters, charts, before/after, source cards, chapter titles).
    • 4 styles, MP4 or transparent ProRes.
    • Batch-rendered from a plan built from the script.
  • herk-edit-kit/: an AI editor for talking-head footage: silence and mistake cutting, storytelling, motion-graphic beats, reels, 406 card drafts and a measured editing playbook.
  • Pointers to the kinetic-reel, painted-cartoon, web-intro and p5-overlay templates inside the skills.

prompts/ — prompts and briefs

  • film-styles/: 51 film-style prompts in one reusable 11-section schema (satellite briefing, archive light table, Swiss motion, data storytelling, isometric infographic, dark keynote, spy titles, glass product, ukiyo-e…).
  • starters/mg-styles-15/prompts/: 15 motion-design style prompts with the source of every film they made, a template for new styles and an AI-jury review rubric.
  • video-prompts/: 64 + 40 curated motion-design prompts and cases from two large collections of Opus 5.5 videos.

docs/ — guides and research

Method

  • techniques.md: the shared method, applied to our tools.
  • reference-only.md: useful material that could not be copied (no licence, or third-party content), with where to find it.

Motion craft

  • guides/: motion fundamentals (iart.ai), field rules for code films (Howseen), effect recipes, news-insert rules, motion tokens, Disney principles in frames.
  • guides/emil-kowalski/: Emil Kowalski's choreography rules (what leads, what follows, what stays still), a build-in-order animation guide with exact curves, and a glossary that names any motion effect for a prompt.
  • guides/reelforge-grammar/: 101 After Effects-style techniques as seek-safe GSAP, 31 verified HyperFrames fragments, and a routing table from scene intent, intensity and mood (English guide to Korean sources).
  • guides/huashu-motion/: rhythm, the camera as a budget, storyboard laws, UI demo patterns, mix ratios and render traps (English guide to Chinese sources).
  • guides/react-bits/: using React Bits backgrounds and text effects in films (loop export, frame-exact capture, picks, licence limits); nothing copied.

Film types

  • guides/explainer-grammar/: eight measured ways to animate a voice-over and which to use for which stretch of VO.
    • Kurzgesagt-style, Vox-style collage, whiteboard, storytime, kinetic type, 3Blue1Brown-style, keynote and finance chart.
    • Twelve rules that hold across all of them.
  • guides/launch-film-grammar/: launch films decided in order with numbers from 47 measured films (registers, structure, type, cuts, sound, review), a sound guide and a film measurer.
  • guides/lemo-opuscar/: directing and pipeline guides for code-made films, and how to make a style your own.

3D and research

  • guides/blender-3d-toolchain/: fourteen Claude × Blender and 3D asset projects: which step each serves, licence, whether it still works.
    • Blender MCP, Blender skills, build123d, Tripo, AutoRemesher, RetopoFlow, PyMeshLab, xatlas, Material Maker, ArmorPaint, meshoptimizer, glTF-Transform and more.
  • research/athemeroy/: a study of 1,000+ agent-made videos, with a production brief, production paths, workflow analysis and data.

Using a skill

Copy a skill folder into %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\ (Windows) or symlink it into ~/.claude/skills/ (macOS, Linux, WSL), then describe the video you want in Claude Code. Details in skills/README.md.

What stays out of git

  • Renders: *.mp4, *.mov, ProRes masters.
  • Unreal caches: DerivedDataCache/, Intermediate/, Saved/, Binaries/.
  • node_modules/, model weights, .env files and large media.

See .gitignore.
